doc.title: Charles Davis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 23, 1997

title: Clarence Henry, Dinah Washington and Billie Holiday
summary: Davis came to New York with Clarence 'Frogman' Henry, worked with Dinah Washington for two years and played with Billie Holiday and Ben Webster in Chicago; vocalists' keys.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: In looking at your information in a couple of different books, starting in the late 50s you went through an amazing list of playing with people at the time — Billie Holiday and Ben Webster.
You had quite an association with Dinah Washington, right?

Yeah, well I worked for her about two, two and a half years. And also, I don’t know if it’s on there, Clarence Henry — speaking of blues — I first came to New York with Clarence Henry. You know, the “Frogman?”
Yeah. I first came to New York with the “Frogman.” And then I went back, that was my first observance of the in-person view of the Statue of Liberty. And then I said well I’ve

got to come back here. And then I came back with Dinah Washington. But while in Chicago I was lucky and fortunate enough to perform with Billie Holiday for about six months, on a local stint that she was dealing with in Chicago, with Billie Holiday and Ben Webster. So that was a pleasure, it was a real learning experience.
Was she — as a player, when you start working with vocalists, you need to start doing things perhaps in different keys than you’ve been used to doing them in, to match.

It was not that exceptional. Most vocalists I work with, it’s just normal keys, it was nothing exceptional. I mean it is different when you deal with vocalists that learn how to play off the guitar. Then that’s when your keys are exceptional.
